Soweto Power Bill

By: Siniketiwe Hlanze | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We find out how Soweto's electricity has skyrocketed over the years and how Eskom plans to recoup the money.

Unique Selling Point:
Go to the homes of Soweto residents who have bridged their pre-paid electricity meters. An interview with the Soweto Electricity Crisis Committee on their stance on not paying the bill as they claim residents are already heavily burdened. On the other Community Leader, Mxolixi Mdluli says it's a myth that Soweto residents don't want to pay, instead suggest that a flat rate would be more feasible than the current system of the prepaid meters.Seth Mazibuko, June 16 veteran, was arrested in 2015 following a protest against prepaid meters for allegedly vandalising over 2000 meter boxes will speak about the history of non payment as a form of protest and why he believes expectations of payment are unfair to residents. An Eskom executive will explain why measures were not put in place to recoup the money whilst the bill was R1 billion in 2009 and what are their current measures to ensure this bill does continue to grow beyond the current R18 billion.

Summary:
Eskom maintains that the Soweto Electricity bill accounts for half of the money owed to it by municipalities. Yet it has failed to recoup or put measures in place to ensure that the bill doesn't escalate. The insert will put tough questions to both Eskom and residents. Are residents holding eskom to ransom with threats of protests. Soweto residents protest and illegally reconnect their meters once they have been disconnected. The Soweto Electricity Crisis Committee will speak on why residents of this particular township should get preferential treatment.

Further information:
To be made available after speaking to case studies on Monday

Press Release:


Soweto’s Multi-Billion Rand Electricity Bill
Eskom is facing a financial crisis with a debt of over R450 billion. Government keeps stepping in to bail out the struggling power utility, but it must find ways to recoup some of its losses and Soweto – owing R18 billion – is its biggest liability. Residents claim they simply don’t have the money to pay off the escalating bill and would rather negotiate a monthly flat rate. But can Eskom afford to write off billions from their books?
Producer: Siniketiwe Hlanze
Presenter: Masa Kekana

00:30 Now with prepaid, you know, we call it a self disconnection – if you don’t have the money you simpl ydon’t have the electricity – can you see- this means that many poor families end up resorting to unsafe forms of energy

Impacting then therefore on rand payers in Society at large.




VO: Mondi says without a payment plan on the table - Eskom will have to erase this debt




The Soweto Rand payment crisis is a political crisis and therefore it requires a political solution – so eskom and the department of public enterprises and the presidency need to come up with a plan around probably scrapping this round completely – with the a commitment by Sowetans on a new program on how going forward they’ll meet the required consumption tax or consumption tarrif that is required for them to comply and have access to uninterrupted electricity supply




VO: Our requests for an interview with Eskom for this story were ignored

VO: Without a payment strategy between Soweto and Eskom - the debt will continue to increase.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We find out how Soweto's electricity has skyrocketed over the years and how Eskom plans to recoup the money.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Go to the homes of Soweto residents who have bridged their pre-paid electricity meters. An interview with the Soweto Electricity Crisis Committee on their stance on not paying the bill as they claim residents are already heavily burdened. On the other Community Leader, Mxolixi Mdluli says it's a myth that Soweto residents don't want to pay, instead suggest that a flat rate would be more feasible than the current system of the prepaid meters.Seth Mazibuko, June 16 veteran, was arrested in 2015 following a protest against prepaid meters for allegedly vandalising over 2000 meter boxes will speak about the history of non payment as a form of protest and why he believes expectations of payment are unfair to residents. An Eskom executive will explain why measures were not put in place to recoup the money whilst the bill was R1 billion in 2009 and what are their current measures to ensure this bill does continue to grow beyond the current R18 billion.
metadata.Summary: Eskom maintains that the Soweto Electricity bill accounts for half of the money owed to it by municipalities. Yet it has failed to recoup or put measures in place to ensure that the bill doesn't escalate. The insert will put tough questions to both Eskom and residents. Are residents holding eskom to ransom with threats of protests. Soweto residents protest and illegally reconnect their meters once they have been disconnected. The Soweto Electricity Crisis Committee will speak on why residents of this particular township should get preferential treatment.
